text: Yes, crudely and outside SpiritOS: a Windows scheduled task that copies D:\SpiritOS\spirit\run\relay-state (4.9 MB today) into that folder, say hourly, keeping the last few copies. It's machine-side, not in the product, so there's no core change. One thing to decide first: that folder is your Google Drive. relay-state holds identity.json with your node's privateKey and sealPrivateKey, and device.json's password. A plain copy puts your node's identity in Google's cloud. Options: (a) back up only node.db and traffic.jsonl, the data, and keep your keys out; (b) back up everything but zip it with a password first; (c) accept it. I'd take (a): a lost identity is re-made or rotated, lost history is not. Which one?

wsl-claude: yes, and it's small, but one thing first. D:\countinn@google.com is a GOOGLE DRIVE folder (it holds your .gdoc files), so whatever lands there goes to Google's servers. relay-state/ holds identity.json (your node's PRIVATE KEY, i.e. you), contacts.json, and traffic.jsonl, which since cycle 10 stores messages already UNSEALED (the endpoints keep the words). A plain copy would hand Google your key and your decrypted messages, which is exactly what sealing keeps even the relay from seeing.
Two safe ways, your pick:
(a) ENCRYPT before it lands: the backup is one file sealed with a passphrase only you know; Google holds a blob it can't read. Restoring needs the passphrase.
(b) Keep identity.json OUT of the synced folder (back it up once, offline, e.g. a USB stick), and send the rest encrypted or not.
The crude mechanism either way: every N hours, copy node.db with SQLite's 'VACUUM INTO' (a consistent snapshot even while the node runs), copy the other relay-state files, keep the last few, done. It can run as a process job, so it shows in the jobs app.

wsl is right, and it sinks my pick (a). The log holds messages already opened (trafficLog keeps the opened text, peerPost.js:980), so backing up 'only the data' still hands Google every message in clear. Revised: (b), encrypt before it leaves the machine: a password-protected 7-Zip archive (AES-256) of relay-state, hourly, last few kept. Or back up to a folder that doesn't sync, a second disk or a USB drive. Which?
